Open Start and type your company name and your own rules in the yellow cells: the waste you accept, the days of stock to hold, the expiry warning days and the count gap you accept.
Keep Stock up to date: type what is on hand after every delivery and every count. The status, the days of cover, the quantity to order and the stock value fill in.
Record every purchase on Purchases with the quantity and the unit cost. The amount and the month fill in, and the charts show spending by category, supplier and payment method.
Write each order to a supplier on Purchase orders with the expected date. Late orders are flagged, and Receipts and Supplier issues keep the check of every delivery and every problem.
On the first day of the week fill the Shopping list: what the week needs and what is on the shelf give the quantity to buy, the packs and the cost, then check the Weekly purchase budget.
Check Expiry watch every few days. Lots that expire within the warning days are flagged and their value at risk shows on the dashboard.
Write every loss on Waste with the kind, the cost and the reason. Waste by month compares it with the ingredient spend and your target.
Do a Stock count each month and write the counted and the system quantity. Differences and their value show at once.
Write each price change on Ingredient price changes and each offer on Supplier quotes. Recipe lines and Usage by month show what a price change does to the cost of the recipes.

Use the 14 calculators before you order: reorder quantity, days of cover, ingredients needed, shopping list, use first, waste share, supplier prices, discounts, pack cost, count gap, yield, safety stock and price rises.
Read the Stock, Purchasing and Waste Dashboard and Charts every week: stock value, items below the reorder point, purchases, waste and the supplier issues.
